reconstructed_captions.35: A hand uses a mallet to strike a pricking iron, marking stitching holes on the leather.
reconstructed_captions.36: The pricking iron is moved along the edge to create a consistent line of stitching marks.
reconstructed_captions.37: A close-up shows the sharp tines of the pricking iron piercing the black leather.
reconstructed_captions.38: The leather piece is secured in a wooden stitching pony.
reconstructed_captions.39: A length of waxed thread is shown with a needle attached to each end.
reconstructed_captions.40: The first stitch is made, passing one needle through the first hole.
reconstructed_captions.41: A hand begins saddle stitching, passing both needles through each hole in opposite directions.
reconstructed_captions.42: A close-up view of the hands pulling the thread tight after each stitch.
reconstructed_captions.43: The stitching progresses steadily along the edge of the leather piece.
reconstructed_captions.44: The final stitches are made, and a backstitch is done to secure the thread.
reconstructed_captions.45: A small pair of scissors snips the excess thread close to the stitching.
reconstructed_captions.46: A lighter is used to carefully melt the ends of the thread to prevent unraveling.
